payload.goal: Make drift mean unrecorded work. Two fixes in one seam: (1) scope the write-back nudge to the session that owes it — today a sibling's activity nags a session that already wrote back; (2) drop command_run from freshnessTotal — speed D-T1 counted it on the false premise that pure reads emit no events, and commands are 57% of every event in this repo. Commands keep being logged; they stop being staleness.

payload.because: T1's stated premise — "pure reads emit no events so they naturally never gate" — is false: an agent reads through Bash constantly, and command_run is 3,277 events, 57% of every event in this repo's records. Two live failures followed. (1) The staleness line cried wolf: a session opened on a cleanly-wrapped record and read "next action may be stale: 12 events since write-back (1 file, 11 commands)" where the 11 were greps from two sessions reading code. (2) Initiative scope nagged the wrong actor: 90 seconds after a write-back, the nudge said "18 record events since the last write-back" — all 18 belonged to a sibling, none to the session being told to write back. T1 had already found half of this, adding session.activity so a sibling's write-back could not exempt a session that did owe one; that closed the false negative and left the false positive open. Per-session accounting closes both and makes the Phase 7 independent-gates law structural rather than an OR. The unattributed term is what session scope alone would lose: `sofar update-task` from a shell lands on "cli" and has no other candidate writer. Classifying commands was rejected because it re-fights the quoting/substitution problem the self-recording scanner deliberately resolves toward logging; deleting them was rejected because the log is the one honest forensic record of what a session ran, and `sofar graph` reads it.
payload.chose: D1: drift = mutation-class only, and gate/nudge scope = sessionDebt(state, session) = the session's OWN unwritten mutations + freshness.unattributed_mutations. command_run is still logged, still per-session in describeActivity, still a graph node — it is dropped from freshnessTotal and from describeFreshness so the headline and its breakdown agree. New fold outputs: SessionState.unwritten (reset by that session's own session_ended, resolved payload session_id ?? envelope) and FreshnessState.unattributed_mutations (counted mutations whose session is "cli" or unregistered).
payload.over: Keeping speed T1's initiative-wide freshnessTotal OR'd with session.activity; classifying commands read-vs-write at the hook (the same losing game the D1 self-recording scanner stays conservative about); or dropping command_run from the log entirely.

plan.goal: Make drift mean unrecorded work: scope the write-back nudge and Stop gate to the session that owes the write-back, and stop counting command_run as drift. Supersedes speed D-T1's premise that pure reads emit no events.
